title: 427. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Solving Elementary Cosine Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Two solutions of a cosine equation in one turn
questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic cosine equation on one full turn in degrees.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\cos x=\frac{1}{2}\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(60^\circ\). Cosine is positive in Quadrants I and IV, so the solutions are \(60^\circ\) and \(360^\circ-60^\circ=300^\circ\). The angle \(120^\circ\) is in Quadrant II, where \(\cos 120^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Find the reference angle, then choose the two quadrants in which cosine is positive.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a cosine equation whose right side is the minimum value of cosine.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\cos x=-1\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The cosine is the \(x\)-coordinate on the unit circle, which equals \(-1\) only at the point \((-1,0)\). This point corresponds to \(x=\pi\). At \(x=\frac{3\pi}{2}\) the point is \((0,-1)\), so the cosine is \(0\).
questions.hint: Find the point of the unit circle whose \(x\)-coordinate is \(-1\).

questions.concept: Cosine equation with a negative value
questions.learningObjective: Solve a cosine equation with a negative right side on one full turn in radians.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\cos x=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\). Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, so \(x=\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{3\pi}{4}\) or \(x=\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{5\pi}{4}\). The angle \(\frac{7\pi}{4}\) is in Quadrant IV, where the cosine is positive.
questions.hint: Use the quadrants in which the \(x\)-coordinate is negative.

questions.concept: General solution when cosine is zero
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution of a cosine equation with right side zero.
questions.question: What is the general solution of \(\cos x=0\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: The cosine is \(0\) at the points \((0,1)\) and \((0,-1)\) of the unit circle, which correspond to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\). These are half a turn apart, so all solutions are \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi\). The formula with \(2k\pi\) misses \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) and its coterminal angles.
questions.hint: Find every point of the unit circle that lies on the \(y\)-axis.

questions.learningObjective: Isolate the cosine before solving a linear trigonometric equation.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(2\cos x+\sqrt{3}=0\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Isolate the cosine: \(\cos x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). The reference angle is \(30^\circ\), and cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III: \(x=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ\) or \(x=180^\circ+30^\circ=210^\circ\). The angles \(120^\circ\) and \(240^\circ\) have reference angle \(60^\circ\) and cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Solve for \(\cos x\), then decide which reference angle has cosine \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

questions.concept: General solution of a cosine equation
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution of a basic cosine equation using symmetry.
questions.question: What is the general solution of \(\cos x=\frac{1}{2}\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: Cosine is even, so \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) and \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) both have cosine \(\frac{1}{2}\), and each repeats with period \(2\pi\). The formula \(x=\frac{\pi}{3}+k\pi\) includes \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), where the cosine is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that \(\cos(-x)=\cos x\) and that the period of cosine is \(2\pi\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the range of cosine to identify an equation without solutions.
questions.question: Which equation has no real solution?
questions.explanation: The cosine of a real number always lies between \(-1\) and \(1\) inclusive. The value \(-1.2\) is below \(-1\), so \(\cos x=-1.2\) has no solution. The value \(-1\) is attained, for example at \(x=\pi\).
questions.hint: Compare each right side with the smallest value that cosine can take.

questions.learningObjective: Count the solutions of a cosine equation on a closed interval of two periods.
questions.question: How many solutions does \(\cos x=1\) have with \(0\le x\le 4\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The cosine equals \(1\) exactly at \(x=2k\pi\). In the closed interval \([0,4\pi]\) these are \(x=0\), \(x=2\pi\), and \(x=4\pi\), so there are three solutions. Both endpoints are included and both are solutions.
questions.hint: List the multiples of \(2\pi\) in the interval, and check whether the endpoints are included.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an equation of the form cosine equals cosine on one full turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\cos x=\cos 70^\circ\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Two angles have the same cosine when their unit-circle points have the same \(x\)-coordinate, that is, when the points are mirror images in the \(x\)-axis. So \(x=70^\circ\) or \(x=360^\circ-70^\circ=290^\circ\). The angle \(110^\circ=180^\circ-70^\circ\) has the same sine as \(70^\circ\), but its cosine is the opposite number.
questions.hint: Points with equal \(x\)-coordinates on the unit circle are reflections of each other in the \(x\)-axis.

questions.learningObjective: Rearrange a linear equation in cosine before solving it on one full turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(4\cos x+2=2\cos x+2\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract \(2\cos x+2\) from both sides: \(2\cos x=0\), so \(\cos x=0\). On the unit circle the \(x\)-coordinate is \(0\) at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(x=\frac{3\pi}{2}\). The values \(0\) and \(\pi\) are where the sine is \(0\), not the cosine.
questions.hint: Treat \(\cos x\) as a single unknown and solve the linear equation for it first.
